rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology section and Tables 4a-c, 5a-b report the project's own on-station and on-farm participatory trials (2005-08) at ten IGP sites plus baseline and end-of-project village surveys (Table 3), with a stated statistical analysis (SAS mixed model).
rows.notes: The study contains no drip irrigation, no subsurface drip, no automated irrigation and no ZT-SSD treatment. The technologies evaluated are laser land levelling, zero/reduced tillage, drill seeding, bed planting, drum seeding, AWD flood irrigation, LCC-based N management and canal lining. Yield effects reported (e.g., zero-till wheat +0.14 to 0.46 t/ha, laser levelling +0.62 t/ha rice) concern tillage and levelling, not drip. Q1 is borderline: the paper is partly a project overview that 'reviews results of a few selected on-station trials' from companion chapters, though it does present project on-farm trial and survey data as its own.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology section and Tables 4a-c, 5a-b report the project's own on-station and on-farm trials and village surveys (Table 3) in Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan.
rows.notes: No tensiometer, soil matric potential threshold, solenoid valve or sensor-triggered automated irrigation appears anywhere in the study. Water savings reported (laser levelling -100 to -280 mm; AWD -233 to -490 mm; ZT-DSR 35-40% less irrigation; canal lining 30-40% savings in Pakistan) come from levelling, tillage/crop-establishment, manually managed AWD and canal lining, not from soil-sensor-based irrigation scheduling. Nothing about doubling irrigation water productivity via automated irrigation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology section and Tables 4a-c, 5a-b report the project's own on-station and on-farm trials and socioeconomic surveys (Table 3).
rows.notes: The study reports no soil-sensor or automated irrigation treatment and therefore no yield effect of such a system. Yield changes reported are for laser levelling, zero/reduced tillage, drill seeding, bed planting, drum seeding, AWD and LCC-based N management (Tables 4a-c, 5a-b); AWD actually showed a yield penalty of 0.3-0.5 t/ha on-station. The claim about tensiometer-triggered irrigation enhancing rice-wheat yields is not supported by anything in this text.

notes: The document is a draft project overview (Ladha et al. 2009, ADB-RETA 6208 rice-wheat ICRM project) with editorial placeholders (e.g., 'this is tentative', 'we need a better reference'). Figures are garbled but tables are present. The paper is partly a synthesis of companion chapters, so Q1 is borderline; it is treated as primary because it presents project on-farm trial data and village surveys as its own, but Q2 is 'no' for all three rows regardless because drip irrigation and sensor-based automated irrigation are entirely absent from the study. The reviewing paper's citation [82-84] appears to be misattributed to this study.
